prompt.adult: Amid Nahum’s warnings of judgment on Nineveh, 1:7 calls the LORD good and a stronghold when trouble comes. Whom does He know?
prompt.child: Nahum says the LORD is good and a safe place in hard times. Who does the LORD know?
prompt.older: According to Nahum 1:7, whom does the LORD know?

verses.text: The LORD is good, A stronghold in the day of trouble; And He knows those who trust in Him.

explanation.child: Look at the last line of verse 7.
explanation.teen: 1:7 says what the LORD is, twice, and then whom He knows. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:3 says the LORD is slow to anger and great in power. 1:6 asks who can stand before His indignation.
teaching.takeaway: The LORD knows those who trust in Him.

prompt.adult: Nahum 1:13 promises Judah that the LORD will break the yoke off them. In 1:15, after the feet of one who brings good tidings appear on the mountains, Judah is told to keep what?
prompt.child: God promises to free Judah from its enemy, and a messenger brings good news. What is Judah told to keep?
prompt.older: According to Nahum 1:15, what is Judah to keep?

verses.text: For now I will break off his yoke from you, And burst your bonds apart.”

Behold, on the mountains The feet of him who brings good tidings, Who proclaims peace! O Judah, keep your appointed feasts, Perform your vows. For the wicked one shall no more pass through you; He is utterly cut off.

explanation.child: Look right after “O Judah, keep” in verse 15.
explanation.teen: 1:15 gives Judah two commands after the good news. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:15 ends by saying the wicked one shall no more pass through Judah. 1:13 speaks of bonds burst apart.
teaching.takeaway: Judah is told, “O Judah, keep your appointed feasts.”

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Nahum 3:8-9 compares Nineveh with another great city that had waters around her and Ethiopia and Egypt as her strength. Which city does Nahum name?
prompt.child: Nahum asks Nineveh if it is better than another strong city surrounded by water. Which city?
prompt.teen: Nahum 3:8: “Are you better than” which city?
prompt.older: According to Nahum 3:8, Nineveh is compared with which city?

verses.text: Are you better than No Amon That was situated by the River, That had the waters around her, Whose rampart was the sea, Whose wall was the sea?
Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, And it was boundless; Put and Lubim were your helpers.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 8.
explanation.teen: 3:8 asks a question and then describes a city. Read the name in the question.
explanation.older: It follows “Are you better than” in 3:8.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:9 says Put and Lubim were your helpers. 3:12 says all of Nineveh’s strongholds are like fig trees with ripened figs.
teaching.takeaway: Nahum asks Nineveh, “Are you better than No Amon?”

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In Jonah 3:10, God saw that Nineveh turned from its evil way and relented. When word reached the king of Nineveh (3:6), he laid aside his robe and covered himself with sackcloth. Where did he sit?
prompt.child: When the king of Nineveh heard Jonah’s message, he took off his royal robe and put on rough cloth. Where did he sit?
prompt.teen: Jonah 3:6: the king covered himself with sackcloth and sat where?
prompt.older: Read with 3:10, where does 3:6 say the king of Nineveh sat?

verses.text: Then word came to the king of Nineveh; and he arose from his throne and laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes.
Then God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God relented from the disaster that He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 6.
explanation.teen: 3:6 lists what the king did after rising. Read the last action.
explanation.older: It follows “covered himself with sackcloth and sat” in 3:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:7 says the decree came from the king and his nobles. 3:9 asks who can tell if God will turn and relent.
teaching.takeaway: The king of Nineveh sat in ashes.

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Nahum 1:8 says that with an overflowing flood the LORD will make an utter end of Nineveh’s place. In the battle scene of 2:6, what are opened before the palace is dissolved?
prompt.child: Nahum said God would bring a flood on Nineveh. Later, in the battle, what gets opened before the palace falls apart?
prompt.teen: Nahum 2:6: what “are opened, And the palace is dissolved”?
prompt.older: Read with 1:8, what does 2:6 say are opened?

verses.text: But with an overflowing flood He will make an utter end of its place, And darkness will pursue His enemies.
The gates of the rivers are opened, And the palace is dissolved.

explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 6.
explanation.teen: 1:8 gives the threat; 2:6 gives two lines of what happens. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:4 says the chariots rage in the streets. 2:9 calls for spoil of silver and gold.
teaching.takeaway: The gates of the rivers are opened.

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Nahum 1:9 says affliction will not rise up a second time. The book’s final verse, 3:19, addresses Nineveh’s injury. What does it say about it?
prompt.child: Nahum ends by talking to Nineveh about its injury. What does he say about it?
prompt.older: Read with 1:9, what does 3:19 say of Nineveh’s injury?

verses.text: What do you conspire against the LORD? He will make an utter end of it. Affliction will not rise up a second time.
Your injury has no healing, Your wound is severe. All who hear news of you Will clap their hands over you, For upon whom has not your wickedness passed continually?

explanation.child: Look right after “Your injury” in verse 19.
explanation.teen: 1:9 speaks of affliction; 3:19 begins with two short statements about Nineveh’s hurt. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:18 says, “Your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria.” 1:12 says, “Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.”

review.notes: Deep Roots stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _deeproots_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Nahum 2:1 mocks Nineveh: “Man the fort! Watch the road!” In 3:14 the city is told to draw water for the siege and fortify its strongholds. Where is it told to go to tread the mortar?
prompt.child: Nahum warns Nineveh to get ready for an attack by making bricks. Where are they told to go to tread the mortar?
prompt.older: Read with 2:1, where does 3:14 tell Nineveh to go?

verses.text: He who scatters has come up before your face. Man the fort! Watch the road! Strengthen your flanks! Fortify your power mightily.
Draw your water for the siege! Fortify your strongholds! Go into the clay and tread the mortar! Make strong the brick kiln!

explanation.child: Look right after “Fortify your strongholds!” in verse 14.
explanation.teen: 2:1 orders the defense; 3:14 gives four commands. Read the third.
explanation.older: It follows “Go” and comes before “and tread the mortar!” in 3:14.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:15 says the fire will devour you there. 2:1 says, “Fortify your power mightily.”
teaching.takeaway: Go into the clay and tread the mortar.

prompt.adult: In Jonah 3:10 God relented from the disaster He had said He would bring on Nineveh. In 4:11 He asks whether He should not pity that great city. Besides the many persons there who cannot discern between their right hand and their left, what else does He mention?
prompt.child: God chose not to destroy Nineveh. At the end of the book, God says He cares about the city’s people and what else?
prompt.teen: Jonah 4:11 ends with what, besides the persons who cannot discern?
prompt.older: Read with 3:10, what does 4:11 add to Nineveh’s persons as a reason for pity?

verses.text: Then God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God relented from the disaster that He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.
And should I not pity Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred and twenty thousand persons who cannot discern between their right hand and their left—and much livestock?”

explanation.child: Look at the very last words of verse 11.
explanation.teen: 3:10 shows God relenting; 4:11 gives the city’s people and then one more thing after a dash. Read it.
explanation.older: It follows the dash near the end of 4:11.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:4 asks Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry?” 3:5 says the people of Nineveh believed God.
teaching.takeaway: God mentions the persons of Nineveh and much livestock.
